name: יַהְוֶה
gloss: he causes to be; or he is (with)
summary: The name of the God of Israel, about 6,800 times, with the short form יָהּ. Its letters are the verb הָוָה “be” (the spelling of Gen 27:29) with the י of a he-form imperfect, the ה kept as the long imperfect keeps it. Read as a causative (hiphil), it is “he causes to be”: the a of יָהּ and of names in ‑יָה is the vowel a hiphil prefix has, where ordinary Hebrew qal has i. Read as a plain stem (qal), it is “he is”. Exodus 3 explains the name from אֶהְיֶה, “I will be”, said first as the promise “I will be with you”, and calls it his memorial to all generations; Isaiah 41:4 sets it with “first, and with the last ones”.

evidence.note: אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ, “I will be with you”: the promise the name-answer grows from.
אֶהְיֶה אֲשֶׁר אֶהְיֶה … אֶהְיֶה שְׁלָחַנִי אֲלֵיכֶם: the answer to “what is his name?”. The same consonants could be pointed as the causative אַהְיֶה.
יַהְוֶה … זֶה־שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם וְזֶה זִכְרִי לְדֹר דֹּר: the name itself, in the third person, “my memorial to generation after generation”.
קֹרֵא הַדֹּרוֹת מֵרֹאשׁ אֲנִי יַהְוֶה רִאשׁוֹן וְאֶת־אַחֲרֹנִים אֲנִי־הוּא: calling the generations; one first, and with the last ones (plural).
Everyone called by my name I created, formed and made: bearing the name and being brought into being go together.
To the fathers he appeared as אֵל שַׁדַּי, but by his name Yahweh he was not known to them.
יַהְוֶה זִכְרוֹ, “Yahweh is his memorial”, as Exodus 3:15.
אֲנִי יַהְוֶה הוּא שְׁמִי, “I am Yahweh, that is my name”.
The short form יָהּ: “my strength and song is Yah”.
הֱוֵה גְבִיר לְאַחֶיךָ, “be lord over your brothers”: the verb הָוָה, with ו, in Hebrew narrative.
Jerusalem is called יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ, the name Jeremiah 23:6 gives the branch: the name borne by the people.
“Who is and who was and who is coming”: the New Testament’s exposition of the name, which reads it as “being”.
“I am the first and the last”, said by the one who died and lives (1:18), as Isaiah 41:4 and 44:6.

note: The two readings are left open here. For the causative: the a of יָהּ and the theophoric ‑יָה/‑יָהוּ; the name spelled with ו (הוה), not the י of the ordinary verb that Exodus 3:14 uses (אֶהְיֶה), which suggests a form set apart from it; and if the name is a hiphil, its own thousands of uses are the stem’s attestation. For the plain stem: Exodus 3:12 אֶהְיֶה עִמָּךְ can only be qal (“be with”), and Revelation 1:8 expounds the name as “who is”. The older Semitic qal prefix was ya-, so the a alone does not settle it. The full form ending in ה is the long imperfect, not the jussive (III-ה jussives drop it: יְהִי, וַיֶּגֶל); the short forms יָהּ, ‑יָהוּ are the apocopated shape. The vowels are not in the Masoretic text, which points the name with the vowels of אֲדֹנָי; the a is known from יָהּ and the names, the second vowel only from late Greek transcriptions (Ἰαβέ); no source for these is registered yet, nor for Josephus’s description of the name on the high priest’s plate as four vowels (Jewish War 5.235).
